newsitem.title: USA: Roth proposes tax incentives for Washington D.C..
newsitem.headline: Roth proposes tax incentives for Washington D.C..

text.p: U.S. Senate Finance Committee Chairman William Roth on Tuesday released a tax plan that includes a series of tax incentives aimed at revitalizing business activity in the District of Columbia.
The bill would designate existing D.C. enterprise communities where the poverty level is greater than 35 percent as a new D.C. Enterprise Zone.
Businesses within the zone would be eligible for a series of tax incentives, including expanded tax-exempt financing and a 20 percent tax credit on wages paid to poor workers.

Roth estimated the cost of the Enterprise Zone incentives at $124 million. Roth's bill also would exclude capital gains requirements for new investment in D.C. businesses that are held for at least five years and meet certain standards.
The bill also would provide $75 million in tax credits to banks and other lenders that provide equity and loans to D.C. businesses in poor areas.
Roth estimated the total cost of the D.C. tax incentives package at $989 million between now and the year 2007.
